question: What follows if agency is attributed to the self only by figurative designation?
premises: A merely figurative designation does not make something what it is called.
Even if a person were figuratively called fire, he would not remove cold caused by snow, hail, showers, and wind.
Real causal power requires more than a figurative name.
inference: Therefore, figuratively calling the self an agent does not give it real causal efficacy.
plain_english: Even if someone were called fire only figuratively, he would not remove the cold caused by snow, hail, showers, and wind.
